players.product: gas & liquid delivery subsystems for etch/deposition tools (Lam, Applied)

quarterly_data.signal: Second quarter revenues of $294.8 million increased 15% sequentially (second consecutive quarter of 15% sequential growth); gross margin 14.1%, up 130 basis points sequentially and above the high end of guidance; EPS $0.34, the highest quarterly earnings in three years; EBITDA up more than 50% sequentially to over $21 million.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $294.8 million (+15% QoQ); gross margin 14.1%; EPS $0.34; EBITDA over $21 million

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 guidance: revenues of $315 million-$345 million, at the midpoint sequential growth of 12% and a year-over-year increase in revenue volumes of 38%; gross margin 14.5%-15.5% as the company keeps driving 100 basis points of gross margin improvement per quarter; EPS $0.40-$0.50.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $315 million-$345 million (+12% QoQ, +38% YoY at midpoint); gross margin 14.5%-15.5%; EPS $0.40-$0.50

quarterly_data.signal: For 2026 Ichor expects revenue growth in alignment with the high end of WFE expectations, an increase of at least 30% from full year 2025; the steepening customer demand ramp indicates sequential revenue growth exceeding 10% in each of the next two quarters and second half revenue volumes at least 25% higher than the first half. Demand drivers unchanged: advanced etch and deposition applications supporting AI infrastructure, gate-all-around architectures, advanced memory and leading-edge process technologies.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 revenue growth at least 30% vs 2025; H2 at least 25% above H1; >10% sequential growth in each of Q3 and Q4

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: Ichor has the capacity today to support $500 million in quarterly revenue ($2 billion annually within the current footprint); with targeted investments (a little more clean room space being executed in the second half of 2026, plus machining capacity) it can expand capacity within the existing footprint upwards of $3 billion annually, more than double the current run rate. Management says neither demand nor manufacturing capacity is the growth constraint today; it is gearing up for a significant 2027 but is not guiding $3 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: capacity $500 million per quarter today; up to ~$3 billion annual within existing footprint after investment

quarterly_data.signal: Isolated part shortages late in the quarter (flow control is the supplier category that keeps the CEO up at night) kept Ichor from recognizing its full revenue forecast by the June 26th quarter end; the revenue shipped literally days after the quarter, and Ichor surpassed $300 million in revenue for the 13 weeks ending July 3rd. Customers are placing POs out six months ahead, which is abnormal, and product qualifications are going faster than normal because customers need to de-risk their supply chain.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue surpassed $300 million for the 13 weeks ending July 3rd; customer POs placed six months ahead

quarterly_data.signal: Malaysia high-volume manufacturing ramp is going exceptionally well: machining and welding have been qualified by both of Ichor's major customers, plus a qualification for a particular part family for commercial space. Proprietary internal content ran at about 25% exiting Q2 and is expected to be around 30% exiting Q3 and around 35% exiting Q4 as Malaysia and additional Mexico capacity come up; this internal content is the main driver of the 100 basis points per quarter gross margin gains toward the 20% target.
quarterly_data.figure: internal proprietary content ~25% exit Q2 -> ~30% exit Q3 -> ~35% exit Q4; gross margin target 20%

quarterly_data.signal: Lithography customer: inventory position has been consistent and Ichor expects to burn through it as it exits Q3, with a return in Q4 and in Q1 in particular; the customer gives a long-range forecast and Ichor sees significant growth in 2027 with that customer, with litho picking up significantly in the first half of 2027 and being additive versus the second half of 2026.

Completed the entire $200 million ATM equity offering during Q2, issuing 2,480,000 shares at an average price of $80.70 per share for net proceeds of approximately $195 million; cash and equivalents $256 million at quarter end, up $167 million from Q1; total debt $120.6 million. Cash from operations was a use of $15.9 million due to inventory investment; capital expenditures $7.8 million, with capex trending higher in the second half while staying within the target of approximately 3% of revenue as clean rooms and machining capacity are accelerated.
quarterly_data.figure: ATM 2,480,000 shares at $80.70, ~$195 million net proceeds; cash $256 million; capex $7.8 million (~3% of revenue target)

quarterly_data.signal: Weldment business is seeing significant growth and recovery after a period of being brought down; Ichor has increased weldment capacity with additional capacity coming online in the second half; chemical delivery, gas delivery and weldments are all executing to what customers need.
